angularDiameterSource: Not measured: no interferometric diameter of Kepler-16 A exists. 0.08 mas is Doyle et al. (2011, Table 1)'s radius, 0.6489 solar radii, at the Gaia EDR3 distance of 75.30 pc.
distanceSource: Gaia EDR3 parallax 13.2806 +/- 0.0284 mas via SIMBAD (2020yCat.1350....0G): 75.30 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.6489 +/- 0.0013 solar radii, mass 0.6897 (+0.0035/-0.0034) solar masses and effective temperature 4450 +/- 150 K from Doyle et al. (2011, Science 333, 1602; arXiv:1109.3432), Table 1, the photometric-dynamical model of the Kepler light curve and the radial velocities of star A: 451,439.73 km at 695,700 km per solar radius; GM is the mass times the JPL solar GM 132712440041.93938 km^3/s^2. Sebastian et al. (2025, MNRAS; arXiv:2505.19718) measure dynamical masses 2-7% higher with SOPHIE; they are not mixed into this record because Doyle's orbits were fitted with Doyle's masses. presentationUp: no spin axis is measured, so the display axis (celestial north at the star) is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Doyle et al. (2011, Science 333, 1602; arXiv:1109.3432), Table 1: effective temperature 4450 +/- 150 K from spectroscopy of star A, https://arxiv.org/abs/1109.3432
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-16 (pscomppars): [M/H] -0.3 dex, from Doyle et al. 2011 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2011Sci...333.1602D/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-16 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.90301, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of Kepler-16 (pscomppars): age 3.8 Gyr, from Q1-Q8 KOI Table (https://exoplanetarchive.ipac.caltech.edu/docs/Kepler_KOI_docs.html)
